segments.title: Brunswick work, Kansas boyhood, and Army band service in World War I
segments.summary: After a recording check, Brewster explains his name, says he ran Brunswick's foreign-release recordings with Glenn Miller and the Dorseys working for him, then recalls his barber father, learning trumpet by ear, the Sears cornet, enlisting in the National Guard band, and Chief Ballardi.

segments.title: Fort Worth pit, vaudeville circuit, and a week with the Dixieland Jazz Band
segments.summary: Brewster goes into vaudeville from a Fort Worth theater, meets his old friend again in Houston, then tells of subbing with the Dixieland Jazz Band, Russell Robinson, his daughter Marcia, and trombonists Miff Mole and Jack Teagarden.

segments.title: New York bands, Meyer Davis one-nighters, and Detroit with Goldkette and Finzel
segments.summary: Talk of Red Nichols, the Memphis Five, short jobs, and Detroit: Henry Thies, Finzel's ballrooms, the Goldkette band with the Dorseys and Venuti, how he got the name Tex, and many sidemen.

segments.title: Goldkette recordings, early radio in Detroit, and touring with Kate Smith
segments.summary: Titles recorded with Goldkette when Victor came to Detroit, Goldkette's background, first radio broadcasts, then Kate Smith's private train, her parties, and her bandleader Jack Miller and Tony Gale.

segments.title: Kate Smith, Washington DC hotels, Masons, jam sessions, and names the interviewer raises
segments.summary: Kate Smith as a young dancer in Washington, the Mayflower Hotel with Meyer Davis, the Shrine band, Louis Armstrong, learning jazz in the Army, Ray Bauduc, Brunswick Records, and a wrap-up with thanks.

segments.title: Interviewer's closing question about his daughter Marcia
segments.summary: Allen asks why Marcia, who loved New Orleans, left for Princeton.
